source.title: Graded commutative algebras: examples, classification, open problems

accepted.question_text: How can one define and develop a geometry for Γ-commutative algebras by introducing an appropriate notion of the spectrum of a Γ-commutative algebra, in a way that extends the well-developed Z2-commutative (supercommutative) case and could provide a new viewpoint on Clifford analysis?
accepted.context_brief: Spectrum and geometry of Γ-commutative algebras

evidence.quote: Among a huge number of open problems we selected one challenging problem that looks particularly promising. A large class of algebras can be viewed as Γ-commutative. This opens a possibility to apply algebraic geometry in order to define geometric objects. The key notions to be investigated are that of spectrum of a Γ-commutative algebra. We think that such a theory could in particular bring a new viewpoint to the Clifford analysis.
